name: Rohit Relan
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Bharat Seats Ltd (JV with Suzuki/Maruti Suzuki)
profile: Indian auto-components industrialist from the Relan family behind Sharda Motor Industries (founded by his father Narinder Dev Relan; brother Ajay Relan is MD there). A chartered accountant, he has run engineering companies since 1986 and leads Bharat Seats, a seating-systems JV of Suzuki Motor Corp, Maruti Suzuki and the Relan family, which recently opened a Gujarat plant.
interesting_fact: Bharat Seats is a joint venture of Suzuki Motor Corporation Japan, Maruti Suzuki India and 'Rohit Relan and Associates', making seats for cars, two-wheelers and even railways.
deep_cut_fact: He has chaired the Indian Polyurethane Association, the Haryana Council of CII and co-chaired the India Japan Business Cooperation Committee; he supports a school for underprivileged girls and is an avid golfer who enjoys Indian music.
notes: Hurun lists wealth source as Sharda Motor Industries (shared with brother Ajay Relan), where he was a non-executive director until ~2020; his operating role is at Bharat Seats. Some aggregator profiles suggest his CMD tenure may have changed in 2024-25; company site still lists him as CMD.

name: John Kristofer Galashan
current_role: Partner and Investment Committee member, Leonard Green & Partners; Director, Life Time Group Holdings and Mister Car Wash
profile: Kris Galashan is a Los Angeles private-equity investor who joined Leonard Green & Partners (LGP) as an associate in 2002 after investment banking at DLJ/Credit Suisse First Boston, and now sits on LGP's Investment Committee. His SEC-reported holdings reflect LGP fund stakes in Life Time (board since 2015) and Mister Car Wash (board since 2014), which LGP took private in a ~$3.1bn deal announced Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: He has overseen LGP's bet on Mister Car Wash since 2014; in 2026 LGP took the car-wash chain private at $7/share (~$3.1bn enterprise value) after taking it public in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Canadian-educated: he earned an Honors Business Administration (HBA) degree from the Ivey Business School at the University of Western Ontario before starting in DLJ's Los Angeles investment-banking office.
notes: Net worth figure largely reflects LGP fund holdings attributed via SEC filings, not personal stake. Mister Car Wash take-private reportedly closed May 2026 (verify); avoid referencing the related shareholder litigation. Low public profile; best route is LGP's office contact form.

name: Mark D. McClain
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Director, SailPoint, Inc. (Nasdaq: SAIL), Austin, Texas
profile: Serial identity-security founder: started Waveset Technologies in 2000 (sold to Sun Microsystems in 2003) and co-founded SailPoint in 2005. He took SailPoint public in 2017, sold it to Thoma Bravo for $6.9bn in 2022, and led it back to public markets in February 2025; he remains CEO as SailPoint pushes into securing AI agent identities.
interesting_fact: He wrote a leadership book, 'Joy and Success at Work: Building Organizations that Don't Suck the Life Out of People' (ForbesBooks, 2020), critiquing perk-driven 'pseudo-cultures'.
deep_cut_fact: After selling Waveset to Sun Microsystems he served as Sun's VP of Software Marketing, then carried Waveset's 'Four I's' core values (integrity, innovation, impact, individuals) into SailPoint.
notes: Accessible, media-friendly founder CEO who speaks often on culture and leadership (book, podcasts). The 'Four I's' values are also described in an Austin Technology Council post: https://www.austintechnologycouncil.org/?p=484

name: Brent M Stevens
current_role: Founder/Manager of Peninsula Pacific and Chairman of Peninsula Pacific Entertainment (P2E); Director, Concrete Pumping Holdings
profile: Los Angeles investor and former Jefferies investment banker (1990-2010; EVP and Head of Capital Markets). He co-founded Peninsula Gaming (sold to Boyd Gaming for $1.45bn in 2012) and P2E, which sold most assets incl. Colonial Downs to Churchill Downs for ~$2.8bn in 2022. Peninsula Pacific also backed Brundage-Bone, now Concrete Pumping Holdings, where he is a ~10%+ holder and director.
interesting_fact: His gaming empire started in 1999 with a single Mississippi riverboat casino, the Diamond Jo in Dubuque, Iowa, bought for $77m; P2E's later assets sold to Churchill Downs for ~$2.8bn in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: Before gaming and concrete, he spent 20 years at Jefferies, rising to Head of Capital Markets and a seat on its Executive Committee; he holds a B.A. in Accounting from USC and a Wharton MBA.
notes: Low media profile. Avoid referencing a past Iowa campaign-contribution legal matter. P2E still pursuing Iowa casino development (Cedar Rapids).

name: Simran Lal
current_role: CEO, Good Earth (Eicher Goodearth) and co-founder/creative director, Nicobar; Eicher Motors promoter-family shareholder
profile: Daughter of Eicher Motors patriarch Vikram Lal and sister of Royal Enfield/Eicher chairman Siddhartha Lal; her Hurun wealth reflects family Eicher Motors holdings. Rather than join Eicher, she joined her mother Anita Lal's luxury design house Good Earth in 2002, became CEO, took it online in 2013, co-founded resortwear brand Nicobar (2016) with husband Raul Rai and later launched luxury label Paro.
interesting_fact: Nicobar is named after the Nicobar Islands in the Indian Ocean; the brand draws on the Spice Route and an island aesthetic, and fabric-hunting and factory visits are among her favourite parts of the job.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Good Earth she had a brief stint at a homewares label; after Good Earth and Nicobar she launched Paro, a luxury brand spanning apparel, jewellery, bed linen and a botanical range.
notes: Design/retail entrepreneur rather than auto executive; some 2024 sources call her 'former CEO' of Good Earth, so confirm current title. Podcast angle: building heritage luxury brands, D2C.

name: John T Stankey
profile: Lifer telecom executive who joined Pacific Bell in 1985 in an entry-level job and rose through SBC/AT&T (CIO, CEO of WarnerMedia 2018-20) to AT&T CEO in July 2020. He unwound AT&T's media bets (WarnerMedia, DirecTV) and refocused on fiber and 5G, buying Lumen's consumer fiber business ($5.75bn, closed Feb 2026) and ~$23bn of EchoStar spectrum.
interesting_fact: Under Stankey AT&T partnered with AST SpaceMobile on satellite-to-phone service and committed $3bn to closing the US digital divide after federal broadband subsidies lapsed in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: He and his wife Shari, both Loyola Marymount alumni (he is LMU '85, finance), endowed the John and Shari Stankey Fellowship, LMU's first faculty fellowship with an interdisciplinary requirement, linking journalism, media, computer science and business (up to $50k/yr).

notes: Very high-profile Fortune 50 CEO; outreach via AT&T Corporate Communications. AT&T is a large data-center/fiber player, so it fits the podcast. The media-contacts page blocked automated fetch, so check it manually. LA native, son of an insurance underwriter.

current_role: Former CFO (to Apr 2026) and director (Apr-Jul 2026) of Fermi Inc.; former CEO of MBO Partners. Current role not publicly stated

deep_cut_fact: A Minnesota-educated accountant, he holds a B.S. in Accounting from St. Cloud State University's Herberger Business School, the base for a 25+ year PwC career that ended as global head of its advisory business.

name: Dennis Degner
current_role: President & CEO, Range Resources Corp (Fort Worth, TX); slated to join EQT's board when EQT's all-stock acquisition of Range closes (expected Q1 2027)
profile: Petroleum engineer who joined Range Resources in 2010 after roles at EnCana, Sierra Engineering and Halliburton, ran operations as COO and became CEO in May 2023. Range is a pioneer Marcellus shale gas producer; on 26 Oct 2026 it agreed to be acquired by EQT in an all-stock deal creating a >$50bn-EV natural gas giant pitched at AI/data-center power demand.
interesting_fact: The EQT-Range merger (0.987 EQT shares per Range share) creates America's largest vertically integrated natural gas producer, >9 Bcfe/d, explicitly positioned for demand-led growth; Degner will join EQT's board.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a gas CEO, his degree is in Agricultural Engineering (B.S., Texas A&M), and he has worked fields across Texas, Louisiana, Wyoming, Colorado and Pennsylvania and published SPE work on deploying new technologies.
notes: Timely guest for energy/data-center angle (Range has an 'Energy for the AI Revolution' section). Mid-merger with EQT, so expect quiet-period constraints until close in Q1 2027.

current_role: Chair, President & CEO, West Pharmaceutical Services (since 2015); Director, Ecolab
profile: Life-sciences executive who spent 22 years at Sigma-Aldrich (1993-2015) running several of its major businesses before becoming CEO of West Pharmaceutical Services, the Exton, PA maker of drug-containment and injectable-delivery components (vial stoppers, syringe components, GLP-1 injector parts).
